recommendedTextbook.title: WABP Junior Secondary Business Studies Book 1
recommendedTextbook.author: Ehiametalor, E. T., Makore, C., & Awoyemi, M. O.
recommendedTextbook.approvedBy: NERDC & Lagos State Ministry of Basic Education

topics.topic: Introduction to Business Studies and Career Opportunities
subtopics: Definition and objectives of Business Studies
Components: Commerce, Bookkeeping, Keyboarding, Office Practice
Career opportunities: Accountants, bankers, marketers, secretaries, entrepreneurs
objectives: Identify the four key component subjects
List 5 career pathways open to business students in Nigeria

topics.topic: The Modern Office: Layout, Sections and Personnel
subtopics: Meaning and functions of an office (receiving, recording, processing, storing information)
Types of office layout: Open-plan office vs closed/partitioned office
Departments in an enterprise: Administrative, accounts, sales, personnel
objectives: State 4 primary functions of a business office
Compare advantages and disadvantages of an open-plan office
Describe roles of clerical staff and receptionists

topics.topic: Office Equipment and Modern Business Machines
subtopics: Classification of office machines: Duplicating, calculating, communicating, recording
Modern digital tools: Computers, photocopiers, scanners, franking machines
Care and safe operation of electrical office equipment
objectives: Identify 6 common machines found in a Nigerian commercial office
Explain business advantages of electronic filing over manual filing cabinets
Demonstrate safe handling and routine cleaning of office equipment

topics.topic: Introduction to Commerce and Aids to Trade
subtopics: Definition of Commerce and its branches (Trade and Aids to Trade)
Types of trade: Home trade (wholesale, retail) and foreign trade (import, export)
Aids to trade: Banking, insurance, transportation, warehousing, advertising, communication
objectives: Diagram the branches of commerce clearly
Explain how banking facilitates domestic commerce in Nigeria
State the role of warehousing in stabilizing market prices during bumper harvests
